criteria.evidence: Every required section is substantive: What it does ("It defines each kind of node that a plan uses: Business Intent, Capability, Functionality, Work and Plan"), Inputs / Outputs ("Out: the ontology file at version 5. For each kind, it gives what the kind is, who reads it and where it lives..."), Rules & behavior (11 rules), six Given/When/Then criteria, Out of scope with owners, and a full ICE section with Goal, Limit, Fails if, Context and Checked by lines.

"Each kind that a plan uses is defined under \"Kinds\"... A play cannot write or check a kind that the ontology does not define. Thus a plan that names an undefined kind cannot be trusted."; "Rules tell what is true when the product is aligned. They never stop a write... a blocked write would lose work that was already found."; "Domain stays under \"Not yet defined\" on purpose, because it is not a level of a plan."

Rules are discrete bullets; acceptance is Given/When/Then: "Given the ontology on this branch, when check_ontology.py runs on it, then it passes with no errors."; the function is stated as behavior, not a user story: "The ontology is the written set of rules for the product model."

Parent capability lists it in one line: "The ontology (fn-597): the written rules for each kind of part and its links, with examples from more than one field." The child adds the named kinds, the inputs (Q1 to Q7, v4, the 2026-10-21 rulings), the per-kind output shape, the edge cases for Domain and Tracker Issue, the depends_on naming note, and testable acceptance.

What: "The ontology is one written agreement, at core/components/memory/standards/schemas/product-os/ontology.md". Why: "A person and an agent both read it, so they use the same words for the same things." Edges: "Changing the ready check script... fn-724 owns that." / "Checking that links point at real nodes, and the rename of depends_on to needs. fn-725 owns those." Terms used are defined in place ("the questions Q1 to Q7 are the fixed list of questions...", "needs means this node cannot be built until that node is done").
